propositions: Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 declare identical 1,000,000-token windows in MODEL_LADDER, making sonnet-to-opus escalation a no-op that retries at identical context limit but at higher cost.

A failed context-limit escalation that moves from sonnet to opus appears successful in logs (rung advanced, retry attempted) but masks the defect (no actual capacity gain), misleading operators into false conclusions about model capability.
The ladder's window figures are correct per live provider API (max_input_tokens), so the defect is in consumption logic, not data; the fix is to filter escalation candidates, not alter the table.

New function escalation_rungs must filter models_at_or_above to exclude rungs whose declared windows are not strictly greater than the last kept rung, preventing zero-gain escalations while keeping models_at_or_above unchanged for other consumers.
Both context-limit retry loops (pass1_with_ladder and run_focused_finder) must consume escalation_rungs instead of models_at_or_above to enforce the escalation guard.

Structural tests must assert that MODEL_LADDER windows are non-decreasing across entries and that escalation_rungs returns strictly increasing windows from any start rung, catching future no-op introductions.
